extracted.intended_audience: Coast Guard contracting officers, MLCPAC contract specialists, Commanding Officers/Executive Officers, and USCG procurement/policy officials
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and oversight criteria for A-76 service contracts within the U.S. Coast Guard, focusing on cost comparisons with the Government Most Efficient Organization (MEO), contract administration, performance, control, funding, and training. Used to assess whether privatization produced savings and was properly administered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are the specifications and contractor performance adequate?
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the specifications and contractor performance adequate for the contracted-out activity? (yes / qualified yes / qualified no / no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether performance meets contract PWS/specifications. Watch for overly rigid specifications that can't anticipate change, variability based on contractor facility management, and unit-level lack of expertise in writing service contract specifications. Note concerns about insufficient training in quality assurance for those monitoring contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the command have adequate control over the contracted-out activity (timeliness)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the command have adequate control over the contracted-out activity (Are responses and remedies to problems timely)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate operational control within contract terms and practical timeliness of remedies. Consider distance between unit and contract administration, centralization of contracting (causing slow responses), and cumbersome indirect contract procedures that reduce flexibility and slow problem resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best performer: military/Government civilian vs. civilian contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: Is this commercial activity best conducted by military or Government civilian employee, or civilian contractor? (Military/Government civilian/Civilian contractor)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider flexibility, instant response capability, influence over priorities, continuity, available civilian workforce, specialty career paths, unit operational needs, and multi-mission capability loss when billets are privatized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command relationship with civilian contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the command's overall relationship with the civilian contractor? (Congenial / Neutral / Conflicting)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess professionalism, responsiveness, project manager quality, and whether contractor activities meet unit needs within the contract. The report found congenial, professional relationships in sampled units despite mixed feelings about A-76 overall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived value of A-76 process
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you believe that A-76 is a good process/idea? (Yes / Qualified Yes / Qualified No / No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture perceptions about the concept vs. implementation. Consider concerns that A-76 can reduce multi-mission capability, hurt career fields (e.g., Subsistence Specialist), cause billet reductions under guise of privatization, and that poor Coast Guard implementation undermines the concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the Government's MEO need more personnel?
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the Government's Most Efficient Organization (MEO) need more personnel to correctly perform the activity? (Yes/No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether MEOs are too lean after billet reductions, whether remaining personnel are overworked or too junior, and whether personnel shortages (e.g., non-rated enlisted shortage) impair performance. If inadequate, consider re-evaluating the MEO and possible recompetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer control over contract cost increases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Contracting Officer has little control over contract cost increases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify causes of cost increases (wage and food price increases, added work, delays in follow-on contract award). Recognize that some drivers (e.g., Producer Price Index, DOL wage determinations) are beyond CO control; plan and estimate readiness-related work in original contracts to limit obligational modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOL wage determinations should be questioned/reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: DOL wage determinations can materially affect contract cost and should be reviewed; inaccurate/low determinations may lead to inappropriate contract awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Support Center Alameda security had a low/inaccurate DOL wage determination that produced contractor personnel costs exceeding the MEO. MLCPAC and COs should question anomalous wage determinations to ensure realistic costing and correct award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MEO cost data must remain available post-award
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Most Efficient Organization (MEO) costs are not available to MLCPAC Contract Specialists after the contract is awarded but should be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain/update MEO cost information post-award so Contract Specialists can determine if Government still realizes savings and can adjust MEOs when contract scope changes (e.g., Support Center Seattle security scope change).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government cost-savings computations must be updated over contract performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall Government cost savings for USCG A-76 contracts may not be accurate because savings are computed based only on initial award price and not updated for actual contract cost changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Savings calculations should be revised during performance to account for actual contract cost increases/decreases, rather than relying solely on the difference between the initial award price and pre-review Government cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding for A-76 contracts must be monitored and adjusted with cost changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding for MLCPAC A-76 contracts by Coast Guard Headquarters does not increase with cost increases; initial funding levels are not monitored/adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HQ should monitor contract actual costs after award and adjust funding to reflect increases/decreases to avoid relying on end-of-year underruns in unrelated accounts to cover overruns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard post-award contract maintenance and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no standard Coast Guard contract post-award maintenance procedure, which has resulted in contract inconsistencies and added work for the Contract Specialist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain complete contract files capable of explaining actions taken. Standardize relief instructions and post-award record keeping. Record and verify deductions for unsatisfactory performance as cost reductions in contract records.

rubrics_metrics.name: COTR training must support day-to-day duties and quality assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: The training received by the Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR) may be insufficient for their assigned duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should go beyond basic contracting principles to include day-to-day COTR duties, lessons learned, and clear methods to ensure quality assurance; current courses were described as vague on QA methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifications should anticipate added work (readiness exercises)
rubrics_metrics.description: Better specifications or estimates can be used to avoid modifications for added work in food service contracts; readiness exercises can create large unanticipated volumes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate readiness exercise meals and other predictable surge needs in original contracts to reduce post-award modifications and unexpected cost increases. Improve initial estimates and PWS drafting to limit added-work modifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly motivated prior military project managers improve contract outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly motivated prior military service project managers make food service contracts work well for the contractor and the customer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, hire project managers with prior military experience or similar backgrounds; interview evidence showed superior cooperation, management quality, and customer satisfaction when PMs had prior military service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Resolutions create significant extra administrative workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Congressional Continuing Resolutions have caused extra work for Coast Guard and Government service contract administrators resulting in an unproductive use of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and plan for continuing resolutions; multiple short-term CRs can force repeated partial obligation modifications (example: three CRs three weeks apart requiring three modifications for every service contract), imposing significant inefficiency on Contract Specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-76 award and return-in-house thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 requires that in order to award a contract to the private sector, the contractor's price must be lower than the Government MEO's personnel related cost by 10%. For an A-76 contract to return in-house, the Government cost must be below the contractor's cost by 10% (for a combined 20% below MEO) plus 25% of the contractor's capital assets cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the A-76 percentage thresholds during award and re-evaluation decisions. Example: Base Ketchikan original negotiated contract price was only 5.4% less than the MEO (not meeting the 10% requirement); a later contract's total cost exceeded projected MEO personnel cost by 37.3%, indicating potential noncompliance with A-76 thresholds or failure to compare against a revised MEO.
